fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Symbolic Literacy as Psychic Self-Defense", "body": "Chance opens by answering listeners who fear being programmed by dark imagery. In his experience, looking at the dark does not harm someone filled with light, because light is awareness, and bringing a culture's symbolic subtext into conscious view lets us choose what we accept and what we reject. He calls symbolic literacy psychic self-defense and suggests the game's artists may have meant their inverted cards as a warning as easily as a subversion. The framing sets the tone for reading the Rider Waite deck beside the Cyberpunk 2077 images, and it returns in his outro, where he wonders whether the original archetypes predate language and symbols altogether."}, {"title": "Archetypes, the Hero's Journey and the Sky Clock", "body": "Asked to define his terms, Lindsey breaks archetype into arch, a ruler or dominating force, and type, a theme, and she treats the major arcana as the ruling themes of a cyclical hero's journey that every life follows. She stresses that each of us is both unique and exactly the same as everyone else. Chance adds that the arch can also point to the starry dome of the zodiac, so the tarot cannot be separated from the sky clock, which describes the seasons as much as human development. In his outro he cautions that the mythic correspondences on the slides come from one book and stay subjective."}, {"title": "Transhumanism as Corrupted Archetypes", "body": "Lindsey reads transhuman as beyond human and calls the urge to get past being human a rotten seed. Drawing on Gnostic lectures, she argues that we do not leave humanity behind but eventually become fully human by accepting our dark potential. Chance defines transhumanism as replacing parts of human behavior or the body with technological improvements, and he claims its deeper aim is to separate people from nature, pointing to the stated goal of some leaders to map minds into a simulation. Lindsey adds that leaning on technology erodes inherent abilities she calls superpowers, which we are letting go."}, {"title": "Inverted Cards: Fool, Magician and High Priestess", "body": "The cyber Fool, Magician and High Priestess are read as deliberate reversals. Lindsey sees the Fool's carefree stance turned into a burdened march beside a dying dog, while Chance notes that an open posture of receiving has become one of reaching to take. Both treat the Magician's knives and masks as the opposite of aligning will with creation, with Lindsey describing four bodies held in balance and Chance linking the masks to a false persona. For the High Priestess, Lindsey sees a crown that wraps and strangles the throat, and Chance adds that the original's blue is missing, which he takes as deliberate."}, {"title": "Venus, Love and the Cyber Emperor", "body": "The Empress is the one card with some beauty left, and both hosts react emotionally. Lindsey sees a triumphant figure who paid dearly to return to a place of suffering, while Chance argues that love cannot be inverted and that nature will survive, even if the corpses of cyborg zombies end up feeding it. He casts Venus as the last holdout. The Emperor then reads to both as technocracy in a card, wired to cords that feed him energy and enthroned too high to reach, and Lindsey contrasts him with strong leaders who stay grounded."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Lindsey Scharmyn (host of the powerful Rogue Ways podcast) joined me for an analysis of the revamped tarot card images hidden in the recent game Cyberpunk 2077. This is not a plot breakdown or game-related show, but instead a look at the synchromystic message from the archetypes contained in this "transhuman tarot." Overall, the episode makes for a great tutorial on the themes found in tarot, astrology, and the universal hero's journey.
fields.Intro Paragraph 2: This was a fascinating and fun, albeit dark, examination and Lindsey made an excellent commentator, thanks to her many years of experience with the major arcana. You'll want to watch the video version of this episode so you can follow along with the slide images we're looking at.

fields.Plus Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "The Cyber Pope as Inverted Gatekeeper", "body": "Lindsey frames the Hierophant as the one who upholds tradition and cares for others, then reads the cyber version as a figure who shows no care at all and blocks the way. Chance notes he is floating, ungrounded, and ties the card to Prometheus, Venus and Saturn, saying the original guards the logos and tests the worthy, while this version siphons from mankind. He argues that control is rooted in fear and conditionals, in his opinion the way demons work on us. Lindsey notes a patch of blue sky behind him, a gatekeeper who decides who passes even if you made it."}, {"title": "The Lovers: Polarity Versus Opposition", "body": "Lindsey insists that polarity is a Hermetic principle and a positive one, because uniting two energies creates something new, whereas the skeleton Lovers show only opposition and a shallow, physical union with the sun muted and the angel absent. Chance reads the touching tongues as a hint that the poles stay connected inside, and he argues that forcing them to be the same on the outside destroys their life giving quality, like poles on a battery. He also reads the burned away skin as a dried out exchange, with each partner sucking the other dry."}, {"title": "Chariot and Strength Without Care", "body": "In the Chariot, Lindsey describes will as choosing how to ride the waves rather than dominating them, and she sees a rider driven by something other than himself. Chance adds that the sphinxes, stars and sky clock are replaced by a dragon and a road. For Strength, Lindsey calls the tattooed lion tamer a show of strength that is really weakness, while Chance reads the missing eye as the removal of care. He offers a numerological reading that he ties to the mark of the beast, which Lindsey calls the most accurate account she has heard."}, {"title": "Conscience, Creativity and the Four Bodies", "body": "Lindsey argues that technology cannot create anything outside the parameters we set, while humans are infinitely creative, and that removing that creative part leaves us a machine. Chance unpacks conscience as knowing together, so repressing it also represses intuition, and he says body energy work is shadow work that mind alone cannot do. Lindsey agrees that every one of our four bodies needs its own practices, and that what feels good and right is the soul speaking. She adds that language was the first voice to skull technology, since a spoken word plants an image."}, {"title": "The Hermit, the Wheel and Healing Yourself", "body": "Both hosts find the Hermit the least corrupted card, with Lindsey seeing a guide who can show the way out and Chance noting artificial light and the harvest time of preparing for winter. The Wheel of Fortune reads to Lindsey as lost control, when the original holds summer, winter, maiden and crone all at once. She closes that every spiritual master said that to save the world you save yourself, while Chance suggests we may eventually leave these images behind for the pure archetypes within, since spirit contains them as their seed."}]

fields.Quotes JSON: [{"text": "Light is awareness, and bringing the symbolic subtext of our world into our conscious mind's awareness is precisely what allows us to choose what we take in and what we reject.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "In a way we're absolutely unique and nothing will ever be exactly like us right here, right now. And another way, we're all exactly the same as everyone else.", "author": "Lindsey Scharmyn", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/266fc9f2-e364-4218-b441-a558779d7c0c/LINDSAY-SCHARMYN.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "We really don't come to truth without dealing with inversion or with lies.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "You don't go beyond human.
